title: Near-linear incremental topological ordering
formal: Does a uniform Las Vegas randomized algorithm maintain a topological ordering of an initially empty directed graph on \(n\) named vertices during edge insertions in expected total time \((n+m)^{1+o(1)}\), with \(O(1)\) worst-case order-comparison queries and \(O((n+m)(\log(2+n))^C)\) words of space for some constant \(C\)? Here \(m\) is the number of edges inserted so far, and every graph in the sequence is promised acyclic.
definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. For each \(n\ge2\), vertices are \([n]\), no parallel edges or loops are inserted, and the complete finite insertion/query sequence is fixed independently of the algorithm’s random bits. Word length is \(\lceil a\log_2(n+2)\rceil\), for a fixed algorithm-chosen constant \(a\) large enough for its storage addresses. After every insertion there must be a total order of all vertices with every edge directed forward. A query on \((u,v)\) returns whether \(u\) precedes \(v\) in that maintained order, with all queries between insertions referring to the same order. It is not a reachability query, and printing a fresh list of all vertices after every insertion is not required. Answers are always correct, and operations terminate almost surely. The update bound means that for every constant \(\eta>0\) there is a constant \(C_\eta\) such that expected initialization plus update time is at most \(C_\eta(n+m)^{1+\eta}\) for every prefix; \(q\) order queries add \(O(q)\) time. No predictions, special graph family or advance edge information are supplied. The target allows the full stated RAM, without an undefined restriction to combinatorial algorithms.
why: Maintaining an actual vertex order remains a central gap between static graph processing and incremental graph maintenance, even as cycle detection itself has become almost linear.

context_blocks.text: The 2025 report distinguishes maintaining a topological order from cycle detection, which already has almost-linear total update time. It records the dense-graph work of Bender and coauthors and sparse-graph bounds with a polynomial overhead.

The report also poses a more specific combinatorial improvement. This card instead formalizes the broader almost-linear ordering target discussed in the researcher list. Prediction-dependent graph maintenance does not establish this guarantee for arbitrary insertion sequences.

progress.text: The report explicitly separates almost-linear cycle detection from the still-slower maintenance of a topological order.
Prediction-based incremental graph results concern additional input assistance and leave the stated unassisted target unchanged.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the same inputs, computation model, space allowance, quantifiers and cost guarantees. A result for a restricted input family or a different model does not decide the full target.

sentences: Directed edges arrive one at a time without creating a cycle.
The algorithm maintains a total vertex order consistent with every edge.
Queries compare two vertices in the maintained order.
The target is almost-linear total update time over the whole insertion sequence.
Fast cycle detection by itself does not maintain the order required here.
